_about: Embedding models the Forge offers, with the two figures ingestion needs from
one: vector width (`dimensions`) and how much text embeds in one pass
(`max_tokens`). Data, not code, for the same reason as model_catalogue.json:
these get checked and corrected, and that should never require a commit to a
Python module. Read fresh on every call, so an edit shows up without a restart.
Every figure was read on 2026-09-25 from the tag's published GGUF header
(`<arch>.embedding_length`, `<arch>.context_length`) on registry.ollama.ai,
and `approx_bytes` is the model layer's size from the same manifest. A
declared value here is what the file says, not what a model card advertises;
where they differ the file wins, because the file is what Ollama runs.
nomic-embed-text's card says 8,192 tokens, its header 2,048.
One deliberate exception: all-minilm keeps 256, the length it was trained on,
although its BERT header allows 512 — a chunk past 256 embeds, but badly.
Declared values are only placeholders. Once a model is pulled, Ollama's
/api/show reports the real figures and services/embedding_models.py prefers
them (MODULES.md 2.2: an estimate and a measurement must never look alike).
A model pulled from outside this list still appears — capability is read from
Ollama, not matched against these tags.
Fields: tag (Ollama tag), label, dimensions, max_tokens, approx_bytes,
languages (starts with 'English' or 'Multilingual' — the Forge filters on
it), recommended (at most one; architecture/04's pick), note.

models.label: Nomic Embed Text
models.note: architecture/04's recommendation. 2,048 tokens is four times M2's largest chunk, so no chunk truncates.

models.label: mxbai Embed Large
models.note: Wider vectors than nomic at a fraction of the context. Fine for 300-500 token chunks, tight above that.

models.label: BGE-M3
models.note: Wide vectors and long context. Over 1GB — check it against the Forge's memory figures.

models.label: all-MiniLM
models.note: architecture/04's 'if hardware is weak'. Tiny and fast; 256 tokens truncates a 500-token chunk.

models.label: Snowflake Arctic Embed 2
models.note: Arctic Embed's multilingual second version. Long context with English retrieval kept strong.

models.label: Snowflake Arctic Embed L
models.note: The large English Arctic model. Same width and window as mxbai-embed-large.

models.label: Snowflake Arctic Embed M Long
models.note: Nomic-BERT base, like nomic-embed-text: the same width and window at the same size.

models.label: Snowflake Arctic Embed S
models.note: Small and fast, with a full 512-token window — unlike all-minilm, a 500-token chunk fits.

models.label: Granite Embedding 30M
models.note: IBM's smallest. The lightest model here with a full 512-token window.

models.label: Granite Embedding 278M
models.note: IBM's multilingual model: English, German, Spanish, French, Japanese, Portuguese, Arabic, Czech, Italian, Korean, Dutch, Chinese.

models.label: EmbeddingGemma 300M
models.note: Google's on-device embedder. Needs a recent Ollama.

models.label: Qwen3 Embedding 0.6B
models.note: Decoder-based embedder from the same family as the chat model. Very long window.

models.label: Qwen3 Embedding 4B
models.note: 2.5GB and 2,560-wide vectors: over three times nomic's index size. Competes with the chat model for VRAM.

models.label: Qwen3 Embedding 8B
models.note: 4.7GB — larger than most chat models here. Only worth it on a machine with VRAM to spare.

models.label: BGE Large EN v1.5
models.note: BAAI's English model; bge-m3 is its long-context multilingual successor.

models.label: Paraphrase Multilingual MPNet
models.note: Sentence-similarity model. Tuned for short paraphrases rather than document retrieval.
